heard: Betelgeuse is not quietly waiting to explode in Orion. Many assume this famous red supergiant sits motionless, simply counting down roughly 100,000 years to its demise. At roughly 10 million years old, it is bloated enough to swallow the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. Yet this giant was violently ejected from its stellar birthplace near Orion's belt. Betelgeuse is an interstellar runaway, plowing through the interstellar medium at 30 kilometers per second. Crashing through cosmic gas at that breakneck speed creates a massive bow shock. When it finally detonates, its daytime explosion will leave life on Earth completely unharmed. Few stargazers realize Orion's brightest shoulder is actually fleeing across deep space.
